newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end higher on PLDT.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end higher on PLDT.

text.p: Philippine shares closed higher on Monday in low volume with PLDT propping up the main index in late trading, traders said.
"We are building a foundation for the market to correct at 2,850. After that, we are on our way to the 3,000 level," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities.
The main index ended 11.27 points, or 0.40 percent, higher at 2,820.72. The index was largely range-bound.
Traders said PLDT pulled up the index in late trade, helped by Meralco B which rose in the late session.
PLDT ended 25 pesos higher at 805 pesos while Meralco B ended one peso more at 149 pesos.

"PLDT is catching up since it has been steady during the market's rise the past seven days," said Helen Alvarez, research director at All Asia Securities. Traders said there is cautious buying on Meralco B.
Losers barely outnumbered gainers 56 to 55 with 79 issues unchanged. Turnover at 1.72 billion pesos was below the daily average of 2.7 billion pesos to 2.9 billion.

"The buying was still on good first quarter GNP. We will likely see narrow range-trading for the rest of the week. Resistance is anywhere at 2,850 to 2,900 points," said Cora Guidote, head of Philippine equities at UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd.
Traders said release of improved May inflation figures -- tentatively due to be announced on Thursday-- will likely put up a cap on any correction that may take place this week.
The main index closed higher for the eight straight session on Monday.
